title: introduce-contract-metadata-and-strict-schema-handling-for-streamed-tool-calls
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds contract metadata headers for streaming events; introduces opt-in strict schema enforcement for tool/function-call results with standardized error IDs; backward-compatible by default; rollout via flag and canary.
description: Motivation: Users integrating structured outputs (JSON schema via response_format) with tool/function calling reported brittle behavior when streamed tool outputs diverged from client-provided schemas. This PR introduces a lightweight contract-metadata layer that travels in-stream so the runtime and client can reach a consensus about which schema variant applies, plus an opt-in strict enforcement mode for tool call results. Goals: 1) Stabilize streaming behavior during tool/function calling so partial tool responses do not cause inconsistent validation errors; 2) Provide clear, machine-friendly error IDs and diagnostic hints when strict validation fails; 3) Maintain OpenAI-compatibility as a default by keeping behavior permissive unless strict mode is enabled. Design summary: We add a new contract-metadata header to the stream envelope (x-contract-schema-id, x-contract-source) which is emitted by the model adapter and echoed by the tool runner when a tool is invoked. The runtime now performs a two-step consensus check: prefer client-specified schema_id, fall back to model-declared schema if the client did not supply one, and in ambiguous cases emit a contract-disagreement event but continue streaming in permissive mode. Strict mode (enabled via response_format.strict = true or response header X-Response-Strict: true) causes the runtime to buffer the final tool payload, run JSONSchema v2020 validation, and if it fails emit a structured error object with fields {error_id, path, expected, received_snippet, severity_hint}. To keep streaming stable for latency-sensitive paths, when strict validation is enabled we allow a short resumable buffering window (200ms default) and do not abort the stream early; when validation ultimately fails we append a terminal validation event and a human-readable suggestion string. Implementation highlights: - Streaming protocol changes: small additions to the stream envelope so existing clients ignore unknown headers; implementation guarded by feature flag 'contract-metadata' for rollout. - Tool runner changes: echo x-contract-schema-id and annotate emitted stdout/stderr chunks with chunk-level schema anchors when available. - Runtime validator: pluggable validator that supports schema version negotiation (v4/v7/v2020) and returns standardized error IDs; validation runs in worker pool to avoid blocking the main recv loop. - SDKs: python and typescript SDKs updated to surface the final validation event and translate error_id into typed exceptions for convenience. - OpenAI-compat shim: when the request includes openai_compat: true, we map our validation event to an openai-style finish_reason and include the structured error in the last chunk under 'metadata' so most existing clients can continue to parse streams. Testing and rollout: unit tests for streaming envelope parsing (server and client), integration tests that simulate divergent schemas between model/tool/client, e2e canary in staging that enables 'contract-metadata' for 5% of traffic, and live traffic monitoring dashboards for contract_disagreement_count and strict_validation_fail_rate. Checklist: - [x] schema header and envelope format defined and documented; - [x] runtime dispatching and buffering implemented; - [x] validator worker and error ID mappings added; - [x] tool-runner echoing implemented; - [x] python and ts SDK hooks implemented; - [x] OpenAI compatibility shim verified; - [x] canary rollout plan created. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is permissive if no strict flag provided; unknown stream headers are ignored by older clients. Risks and mitigations: risk of added latency when strict mode enabled; mitigated by buffered window + worker pool and a per-tenant throttle; risk of increased error noise during early rollout; mitigated via canary and metrics gating. Related work: builds on prior schema checkpointing work (see ENG-6233) and improves on the 'resume token' approach by adding explicit contract metadata to stream events. Docs: updated redwood docs with examples for response_format.strict and SDK mapping for error_id. Rollout: feature-flag rollout over two weeks with observability thresholds for rollback.

review_comments: Ethan Li: Can we avoid blocking the main streamer on validation? The worker pool approach looks good but add quotas per-tenant.
Maya Chen (author): Added per-tenant quota and metrics; validation queue depth exposed as metric.
Sofia Ramirez: SDK error_id string format should be stable. Please include semantic versioning for error catalogue.
Maya Chen (author): Added error_catalog_version header and updated SDK mapping code to include catalog_version in exceptions.
Victor Huang: What about non-json tool outputs (plain text)? Shouldn't validation be best-effort only?
Maya Chen (author): We skip validation for non-json content-types; added detection and clear audit log lines for skipped validations.
